title: Book Two · Chapter 135: The Extra Hour
story:
During the summer holiday, Dad comes home late twice in one week. On the third evening, Ronan watches the green door until the light begins to fade.

Mum puts supper on the table.

“We can begin,” she says. “He knows where his bowl is.”

Ronan takes a small mouthful. He hopes Dad will have time for him this evening.

When Dad arrives, his shirt is damp. He washes, sits down, and reaches for the water.

“Another job?” Ronan asks.

“An old one. I needed to correct a shelf.”

“Does Mr Sun pay you for the extra hour?”

“Not this one. The wrong measurement was mine.”

Ronan sets down his chopsticks.

“So you work and get nothing?”

“I get the shelf right.”

“But you lose time.”

“Yes.”

Ronan thinks of the brown notebook. “You said you count your time now.”

“I do. I still make mistakes.”

Mum brings Dad's bowl. “Eat first. You can argue after the rice.”

Dad takes a mouthful. Ronan waits, but the anger stays with him.

“Mr Sun should help.”

“He did. He kept the space clear and spoke to the customer. The measurement is my part.”

Ronan looks away. He wishes someone else could correct the shelf. Then Dad could come home sooner.

After supper, Dad sits near the door. Ronan brings the water. He does not ask another question until Dad has taken it.

“Will you work late tomorrow?”

“No. The shelf is done.”

“Can we go to the square?”

“Yes. After my usual work.”

The next evening, Dad arrives on time. Ronan has the ball ready, but Dad asks for ten minutes to sit.

“You said after work.”

“This is after work. I need ten minutes.”

Ronan sits on the step. He rolls the ball between his shoes. Dad drinks water and takes off his work shoes. Then he puts on lighter ones.

“Ready.”

They reach the square as the shadows grow long. Dad cannot run as fast as Leo, but he can send a straight ball. Ronan catches it high over his head.

“Good hands,” Dad says.

“Good throw.”

They play a slow game. Each good catch gets one point. At twenty, Dad stops counting. Ronan makes him begin again from one.

On the way home, Dad puts an arm around his shoulders. It is heavy and warm. Ronan leans into it for three steps. At the narrow lane, Dad lets his arm fall. They walk one behind the other. Ronan carries the ball, and Dad carries the empty bottle.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

measurement＝测量；correct＝修正；usual＝通常的；shadow＝影子。

## 理解问题

1. Dad为什么没有额外一小时的报酬？
2. 父子对休息十分钟有什么小分歧？

## 读句子

**Mum / brings / Dad's bowl.** Mum／端来／Dad的碗。
